data.title: GLOBAL MARKETS-Stocks slip as dollar heads for weekly loss
data.description:
(Updates headline and prices throughout, adds oil settlement)

* US dollar heads for weekly loss on lower US Treasury yields

* Bond markets stabilise after rush for safe havens on Thursday

* Investors worry about debt risks in AI-related stocks

By Chibuike Oguh and Elizabeth Howcroft

NEW YORK/PARIS, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Global stocks fell modestly on Friday as markets stabilised after a sharp tech-led selloff, while the dollar headed for a weekly loss.

Markets have been rattled this week by concerns over higher interest rates and the debt-fuelled financing behind the AI boom, triggering a selloff in technology and chip stocks.

Traders increased bets on further US rate hikes after stronger-than-expected inflation data was released on Wednesday, while investors piled into Treasuries and other government bonds.

On Wall Street, the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq were trading down and were headed for weekly losses. The Dow was lower after reversing early gains but was still set for a weekly gain.

Technology and communication services were driving losses while the top gainers were utilities and energy stocks.

CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) shares shed 13% and were on track to lose nearly 26% this week amid increasing investor scrutiny of the financing for the massive AI infrastructure buildout.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.57%, the S&P 500 lost 1.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.3%.

The MSCI World Equity Index lost 0.54% and was set for a weekly loss. European stock indexes, hit less hard by Thursday's selloff, gained, with the STOXX 600 adding 0.72%. London's FTSE 100 rose 0.38%.

"We're starting to see some cracks in the financing of data centers because you're not too sure who's going to be the winners," said Tom Plumb, portfolio manager at Plumb Balanced Fund.

"Our view is that there's going to be some really significant winners. But you have to be careful on the financing capability because companies don't get into trouble because their assets don't exceed their liabilities. They get into trouble when they have liquidity issues."

Asian stocks mostly rose, and bond markets steadied, with investors reversing some of the previous session's moves.

Indonesian equities suffered their biggest drop since 1998 after index provider MSCI said the country's market no longer merited emerging-market status and outlined plans to remove it from key indexes tracked by funds.

DOLLAR FALLS, BONDS RECOVER

The dollar index fell 0.21% and was on track for its first weekly decline after four weeks of gains, as lower Treasury yields reduced the currency's appeal. Further worries about AI would push the dollar down further, analysts said.

The euro rose from its recent 17-month low. It was last up 0.1% at $1.12315.

The Japanese yen weakened 0.03% against the greenback to 158.05 per dollar.

European government bond yields edged higher, while US bond yields reversed earlier declines. Germany's 10-year yield rose 4.36 basis points to 3.453%. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes rose 2.13 basis points to 5.108%.

Even so, yields have eased this week as investors sought the safety of government debt amid concerns about AI-related companies' finances. G7 government bond markets were on course for their strongest weekly performance since late May.

Brent crude futures rose 3.72% to settle at $109.86 a barrel and were headed for a second straight weekly gain amid concerns over Middle East supplies. Attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have surged in the past 10 days.

Gold gained support from the weaker dollar, rising 0.25% to $4,159.69 an ounce.

(Reporting by Chibuike Oguh, Kevin Buckland and Elizabeth Howcroft; Editing by Ros Russell, Mark Potter, Andrew Heavens, Rod Nickel)

data.title: Update: Market Chatter: NBA Restricts Certain Types of Bets for New Season
data.description:

The National Basketball Association has instructed sportsbook partners, including DraftKings ( DKNG ) and Flutter Entertainment's ( FLUT ) FanDuel, to stop offering certain types of bets this season, ESPN reported Friday, citing a league memo.

The restrictions include a player prop parlay used by gamblers in betting scandals, the report said. The league also prohibited bets on the opening-tip winner, players to miss specific shots and under wagers on players expected to play fewer than 12 minutes, the report added.

NBA said there is balance between removal of problematic bet types and ensuring not moving the activity into the illegal market, according to the report.

"The legalized sports betting industry is built on a foundation of dialogue and collaboration with our league partners and the states in which we operate. We remain unwavering in our commitment to building a legal and regulated market that roots out abuses by those who seek to undermine fair competition and damage the integrity of the games we love," a FanDuel spokesperson said in an emailed statement to MT Newswires.

DraftKings ( DKNG ) and the NBA did not immediately respond to requests for comment from MT Newswires.

data.title: UK's FTSE 100 logs strongest week in six months on defensive-sector rally
data.description:
(Updates to markets close)

Oct 16 (Reuters) - Britain's blue-chip stocks had their best week in six months, as investors flocking to defensive sectors offset a rout in AI-linked stocks, while finance minister John Healey's reassurances on fiscal discipline also helped risk appetite.

The export-heavy FTSE 100 closed 0.38% higher at 10,881.90 points, logging a weekly gain of 3.1%, the biggest since early April, while the midcap FTSE 250 gained 0.45%.

* UK's large-cap ETFs attracted $3.38 billion in estimated net inflows year to date, already the biggest annual total since 2020, data from Morningstar showed

* "Flows into passive funds typically follow performance, but they also reflect investors looking to diversify away from US mega-cap technology and broaden their equity exposure," said Michael Born, an analyst at Morningstar

* Consumer staples supported gains. Cigarette maker British American Tobacco ( BTI ) rose 2.1%, while Johnnie Walker owner Diageo ( DEO ) gained 1.9%

* The beverages and medical equipment and services sectors advanced 7.8% and 6.9%, respectively,in the week

* Homebuilders jumped over 6% in the week after Healey reaffirmed his commitment to fiscal discipline on Thursday

* Banks were muted on Friday, recovering from early losses triggered by a report that Healey was likely to tax the lenders in the budget

* Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said signs of second-round inflation were limited ahead of next week's inflation data

* Traders are pricing in four BoE rate hikes over the next 12 months, according to LSEG data

* Defence stocks extended a strong run on the day: BAE Systems and Babcock International ( BCKIF ) rose 2.6% and 3.6%, respectively

* THG had its best week in six months, surging 30% after the e-commerce firm raised its annual adjusted core profit forecast on Thursday

data.title: FAA set to approve Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week, sources say
data.description:
* FAA completed key Type Certification Board safety review on Friday, sources say

* Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, about 30% of 737 backlog

* FAA said October 2 navigation software glitch posed no safety concern

By David Shepardson and Dan Catchpole

WASHINGTON, Oct 16 (Reuters) - The Federal Aviation Administration is set to approve the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week, after completing a key safety review on Friday, three people familiar with the matter said.

The review by the Type Certification Board - made up of FAA management team members - is a final step before the agency decides on certification. The MAX 10 is a larger variant of Boeing's ( BA ) best-selling 737 MAX and its expected approval marks a key milestone for the US planemaker.

Boeing ( BA ) has faced a more stringent certification process since two fatal MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019, as well as scrutiny of the company's production and quality systems after a January 2024 mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9.

Asked for comment, the FAA said, "Safety dictates the certification timeline." Boeing ( BA ) referred questions to the FAA.

The FAA in August gave long-awaited ​approval to the smaller 737 MAX 7 after reviewing the plane for more than eight years. Boeing ( BA ) at one point planned to start delivering the MAX 10 in 2020.

A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that arose in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and 10.

The delays have helped European rival Airbus' A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market. Boeing ( BA ) has said the MAX 10 will be a major cash-flow driver in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies.

Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for about 30% of Boeing's ( BA ) outstanding 737 backlog. The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery.

The bigger plane that can carry more passengers is crucial to several airlines' growth plans. Major customers for the MAX 10 include United Airlines, Alaska, Ryanair, Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) and American Airlines ( AAL ).

A glitch with the latest update of the 737 MAX's navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing ( BA ) disclosed it in late September. However, the FAA determined on October 2 that it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing ( BA ) to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the plane.

Boeing ( BA ) is still working on certifying the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is already six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in 2027.

(Reporting by David Shepardson in Washington and Dan Catchpole in Seattle; Editing by Matthew Lewis)

data.title: Avenue Capital emerges as frontrunner for stake in Serie A media rights venture, sources say
data.description:
* Targets 10% stake for €320 million as common equity, sources say

* Offer emerged as best option at Friday's meeting, sources say

* Rival bid pegs higher valuation under structured equity deal,

* sources say

* Bids to examined further in coming weeks, sources say

*

By Elvira Pollina

MILAN, Oct 16 (Reuters) - Private equity firm Avenue Capital has emerged as the leading bidder for a minority stake in the company that will hold the international media rights of Italy's top soccer league Serie A, two people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters.

Serie A is exploring the sale of a stake in a company that will hold its international broadcasting, sponsorship and betting rights and last month it received final bids from private equity firms.

Serie A clubs met on Friday for an initial review of the bids, the two people said.

New York-based Avenue Capital is targeting a stake of 10% in the media company for €320 million, the people said, which would put the overall valuation of the venture at €3.2 billion.

Avenue is in the lead despite the fact that some rival bidders have offered to pay more because its offer is structured as a common equity investment, without the protections on future cash flows sought by some of the competitors, one of the two people said.

The person added that Carlyle and Nextalia, which teamed up to submit a joint bid, had offered around €650 million for a stake of roughly 17%, valuing the venture at about €3.75 billion.

The Avenue Capital offer will be examined more closely in the coming weeks by the clubs, the people said, cautioning that there is no final decision on the matter.

Avenue Capital and Serie A declined to comment. Carlyle and Nextalia were not immediately available to comment.

Any deal requires the backing of at least 14 of the league's 20 clubs.

Home ⁠to Inter Milan, AC Milan and Juventus, the Italian league has been struggling in recent years to sell its media rights abroad, as broadcasters' interest ​dwindled due to a crowded fixture list dominated by the expanded UEFA ​Champions League and ⁠the popularity of England's Premier League.

The Serie A international media unit generates sales of around €250 million a year, a fraction of those yielded by Premier League and Spain's LaLiga, according to data from ⁠European soccer ​body UEFA.

(Reporting by Elvira Pollina; Editing by Valentina Za)

data.title: CoreWeave bond rout tests market's math on AI buildout
data.description:
PROVIDENCE, Rhode Island/NEW YORK, Oct 16 (Reuters) - A sharp decline in CoreWeave's ( CRWV ) bonds this week is emerging as a test of investors' willingness to keep financing the massive buildout of AI infrastructure, as rising borrowing costs and scrutiny of debt-funded expansion hit the sector.

Analysts and portfolio managers said the selloff in the data center operator's debt carries more significance than a concurrent rout in its shares because it may signal a broader reassessment of the risks tied to financing AI projects that may take years to generate revenue.

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) bonds issued in June at a yield of 9.675% have plunged in value, sending their yield to 15% this week.

"CoreWeave ( CRWV ) is absolutely the canary in the coal mine" for a market segment that is coming under more stress, said Max Frumes, global head of distressed and leveraged finance at 9fin, a fintech corporate credit data and analytics company.

"This is going to be a turning point in the pricing and availability and structure of credit that's supporting the AI boom," said Frumes, who believes that other AI-linked debt will follow CoreWeave ( CRWV ) into distressed territory. "It's going to get more expensive. There will be a lot more scrutiny and probably some pushback from investors."

CoreWeave ( CRWV ) shares fell 15.1% from Monday's open through Thursday's close, despite a 6% gain on Thursday after a vote of confidence from partner Nvidia. The decline was broadly in line with weakness in other so-called neocloud companies such as Nebius and Iren.

Credit investors said they already are becoming more selective.

"We're definitely taking another look at our exposures across the AI infrastructure space, particularly where the risks are concentrated and whether we're being adequately compensated for taking them," said John Han, a portfolio manager at fixed-income asset management firm F/m Investments.

F/m's portfolio contains unsecured CoreWeave ( CRWV ) bonds in one of its exchange-traded funds, but only because they make up part of the index tracked by the ETF. At their current yields those bonds "certainly deserve another look," Han said. He generally prefers to invest in high-yield securities via special purpose vehicles that may offer lower yields but also more collateral and less risk.

"The market is being very selective and really singling out anything that has more leverage, and (that may be) in a bit more challenging operating environment," said Larry Holzenthaler, senior portfolio manager of fixed income at Catalyst funds.

To Holzenthaler and other investors, what the markets are witnessing now is an overreaction as sentiment shifts from being overly upbeat to downright bearish.

In June, the risks driving the selloff -- the sheer size of the funding needs, the leverage, the reliance on outside financing, the risk that the GPUs (graphics processing units) being purchased for data centers would be obsolete before the new facilities could open -- were merely overlooked or downplayed.

"A few months ago, I would have said people were just too optimistic around AI," Holzenthaler said.

Deutsche Bank global head of macro and thematic research Jim Reid sees the market entering a new phase in which debt financing is becoming increasingly important.

"As we move to a capex cycle funded out of debt rather than simply free cash flow, we have to increasingly respect the credit price action," Reid wrote in a recent report. "AI financing costs aren't dramatic overall, but there are worrying themes at the edges."

Vanguard bond portfolio manager Brad Collins said assessing AI-related debt has become more challenging as issuers bring increasingly large and varied offerings to market, often forcing investors to make decisions in days or even hours.

Rising inflation has pushed financing costs higher overall and fueled concern about what lies ahead for mammoth AI capital spending plans. Then there is the growing political controversy surrounding the construction of data centers.

Even one of the tech sector's stalwarts allows that the road ahead may be bumpy at times. Dan Ives, partner and technology analyst at Yorkville Ives, an investment firm, estimates that 5% to 10% of planned projects ultimately will not be built.

"The growing noise around data center permitting and midterm rhetoric on power prices has given investors another reason to step back," Ives said.

(Reporting by Suzanne McGee in Providence, Rhode Island and Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss in New York; editing by Colin Barr and Cynthia Osterman)

data.title: US annual budget gap hits nearly $2 trillion, largest in 5 years
data.description:
* Debt-service outlays climb 12% to record $1.36 trillion, Treasury data shows

* Net tariff receipts fall $22 billion after $145 billion of refunds

* Fiscal 2026 deficit equals estimated 6.2% of GDP versus 5.8% in 2025

By Dan Burns

Oct 16 (Reuters) - The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to nearly $2 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures showed on Friday.

Continued increases in spending for social benefits programs like Social Security and Medicare and a $48 billion jump in defense spending also factored into the increase.

The $1.99 trillion deficit for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, was up from $1.78 trillion in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third-largest annual deficit ever.

Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year.

Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago.

Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion.

Defense spending for the year rose by 6% to $917 billion. A US Treasury official said it was not clear how much of the increase could be attributed to the war Trump and Israel started against Iran earlier this year.

The Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025.

For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: Nasdaq Posts Worst Weekly Drop in Months as Dow Edges to a Narrow Gain
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stock Preachers  News Commentary - Wall Street closed a volatile week split sharply down the middle. The Dow finished Friday at 52,134.63, down 0.08% on the day but still up 0.93% for the week, while the Nasdaq Composite tumbled 1.28% Friday and 3.64% for the week, its worst stretch in months. The S&P 500 fell 1.43% weekly and the Russell 2000 dropped 2.43%. The VIX climbed to 17.02 and the VXN jumped to 22.89, underscoring the growing divide between mega-cap tech weakness and broader market resilience. Active Companies from around the markets with current developments this week include: Lockheed Martin ( LMT ) , Beretta Holding S.A. , Truist Financial Corporation ( TFC ) , CLPS Incorporation , and Orvana Minerals Corp. ( ORVMF ) .

Friday's session showed the market's split personality in real time. The S&P 500 slid 0.58% to 7,699.50, pulling back from its week high of 7,821.67 and testing its 50-day EMA support near 7,681.97. The Nasdaq's 1.28% Friday drop capped a week that erased nearly 1,000 points, closing at 26,370.53 against a week high of 27,376.66, with RSI14 down to 40.4, signaling fading momentum.

Small caps lagged further, with the Russell 2000 down 1.03% Friday and 2.43% on the week, closing at 2,738.83 with an RSI14 of just 33.5, deep in weaker territory. The Dow bucked the trend, holding a 0.93% weekly gain and an 8.47% year-to-date advance, closing just under resistance at 52,281.19 and above its 50-day EMA support at 52,017.10.

Commodities sent mixed signals too. Gold slipped 0.10% for the week to $4,186.50 an ounce while silver fell 4.38% to $57.51. WTI crude jumped 4.17% weekly to $97.65 a barrel, up 70.06% year-to-date, while the 10-year Treasury yield eased 13 basis points to 5.11%, even as it ticked up 2 basis points on the day.

The full report breaks down the key support and resistance levels traders are watching next week along with sector-by-sector sentiment across the divided market.

CONTINUED... Read this and more news at: https://stockpreachers.com/articles/a-week-that-split-the-market-right-down-the-middle/

In other industry developments and happenings in the market this week include:

Lockheed Martin ( LMT ) Lockheed Martin ( LMT ) delivered a C-130J-30 Super Hercules aircraft to the U.S. Navy at its Marietta, Georgia facility on Oct. 15, marking the start of its transformation into the E-130J Phoenix II, the Navy's next-generation TACAMO mission platform for airborne nuclear command and control.

The aircraft will next be transferred to Northrop Grumman, the mission systems integrator, to complete the conversion. "This delivery marks a historic milestone for the U.S. Navy, Lockheed Martin ( LMT ), and the nation's strategic communications network," said Trish Pagan, vice president of Lockheed Martin's ( LMT ) Air Mobility & Maritime Missions.

The delivery revives the link between the TACAMO mission and the Hercules family, which previously flew the mission via the EC-130Q variant from 1963 until 1993.

Beretta Holding S.A. Beretta Holding announced preliminary results of its cash tender offer for shares of Sturm, Ruger & Company ( RGR ) at $44.80 per share. The offer, which expired Oct. 15, sought up to 2,400,184 shares but drew 3,589,647 shares validly tendered, excluding 2,652,256 shares tendered by notice of guaranteed delivery.

Because the offer was oversubscribed, Beretta Holding estimates a preliminary proration factor of approximately 38.45%, subject to confirmation by the depositary following the guaranteed delivery period.

"This investment represents a significant milestone for Beretta Holding. It marks our first participation in a publicly listed company and opens a new chapter in our development as a long-term investor in the U.S. capital markets," said Pietro Gussalli Beretta, Chairman and CEO of Beretta Holding.

Truist Financial Corporation ( TFC ) Truist Financial Corporation ( TFC ) reported its third quarter 2026 results, with details available through its earnings release, investor presentation and Quarterly Performance Summary posted to the company's investor relations website.

The company hosted a live earnings call at 8 a.m. ET the same day, with a replay made available on its website for 30 days.

Truist describes itself as a top-10 commercial bank with total assets of $554 billion as of Sept. 30, 2026, offering consumer and small business banking, commercial and corporate banking, investment banking, wealth management, payments and specialized lending.

CLPS Incorporation CLPS Incorporation reported full fiscal year 2026 revenue growth of 4.7% year-over-year to $172.2 million, and second-half revenue growth of 6.6% to $87.1 million, despite revenue pressure from the downsizing of a key client's China Solution Centers.

Revenue from customized IT solution services surged 113.9% year-over-year to $5.9 million for the full year, while revenue generated outside mainland China rose 47.5% to $62.7 million, with Hong Kong SAR up 61.0% to $23.2 million and Japan up 122.7% to $4.5 million.

"Fiscal 2026 was a pivotal year of structural transition and resilience for CLPS ( CLPS )," said Raymond Lin, Chief Executive Officer of CLPS ( CLPS ). "Since becoming a publicly traded company in 2018, we have expanded our topline from $48.9 million to $172.2 million, delivering a robust 17.0% compound annual growth rate over the past eight years."

Orvana Minerals Corp. ( ORVMF ) Orvana Minerals Corp. ( ORVMF ) reported fourth quarter and fiscal 2026 production results, with consolidated FY2026 production of 45,160 gold equivalent ounces, comprised of 39,282 gold ounces, 3.1 million pounds of copper and 112,499 silver ounces.

Orovalle produced 37,775 ounces of gold and 2.9 million pounds of copper in FY2026, exceeding gold production guidance of 34,000 to 37,000 ounces and landing within copper guidance of 2,700 to 3,000 thousand pounds. EMIPA produced its first dore and copper cathodes from the expanded Don Mario Plant during the quarter but came in below the company's FY2026 guidance, which was withdrawn on September 17, 2026.

"Looking ahead to FY2027, our focus remains on sustaining disciplined production performance and operational efficiency while managing inflationary cost pressures arising from broader global conditions and continued workforce challenges."

data.title: Air Canada, United Airlines to expand Canada-US network with new summer routes

Oct 16 (Reuters) - Air Canada ( ACDVF ) on Friday said it will launch new trans-border routes in partnership with United Airlines for summer 2027, expanding non-stop access to US destinations and enhancing connections across the country.

The carrier will launch services from Toronto to Louisville, Montreal to Indianapolis and Edmonton to Newark during the season, while also increasing capacity on its Edmonton-San Francisco route by deploying larger Airbus aircraft.

Here are more details:

-- The expansion comes as Air Canada ( ACDVF ) and United Airlines seek to deepen their presence in the Canada-US market through their joint business agreement, despite softer cross-border demand in recent months

-- The new routes support both business and leisure travel, while advancing Air Canada's ( ACDVF ) strategy of connecting US passengers through its Canadian hubs to destinations in Europe and Asia, the Canadian airline said

data.title: US fiscal 2026 budget deficit rises to $1.99 trillion, largest in 5 years
data.description:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - The US budget deficit rose by $217 billion to $1.99 trillion in the 2026 fiscal year, fueled in part by tariff refunds and record spending to service the nation's more-than $40 trillion in debt, marking the largest budget shortfall in five years, Treasury Department figures reported on Friday showed.

The results for the year ended September 30, the first full budget year of President Donald Trump's second term, compared to a $1.78 trillion deficit in fiscal 2025. It was the largest shortfall since fiscal 2021's $2.77 trillion budget gap, then fueled by COVID-19 pandemic relief spending, and is the third- largest annual deficit ever.

Total receipts for fiscal 2026 were a record $5.40 trillion, up $169 billion, or 3%, from the $5.24 trillion in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 outlays also were a record at $7.40 trillion, up $386 billion, or 6%, from the $7.01 trillion in the prior fiscal year.

Debt-service outlays totaled a record $1.36 trillion, climbing by $144 billion, or 12%, a spending category now eclipsed only by Social Security and the combined outlays for Medicare and Medicaid. Total US debt breached the $40 trillion milestone about two months ago.

Another driver of the widening shortfall was a $22 billion drop in net tariff receipts following a Supreme Court ruling this year negating a large portion of the tariffs Trump had imposed during his first year in office. That triggered $145 billion of tariff refunds over this year, resulting in an 11% decline in net tariff income to about $173 billion.

A U.S. Treasury official said the department calculated an estimated deficit-to-GDP ratio of 6.2% for fiscal 2026, but declined to say what GDP estimate was used. This figure compares to an actual 5.8% deficit-to-GDP ratio for fiscal 2025.

For the 2026 fiscal year's final month of September, the Treasury reported a deficit of $27 billion versus a $198 billion surplus a year earlier.

(Reporting by Dan Burns; Editing by Andrea Ricci)

data.title: Trump says neither he nor Musk responsible for Ukraine loss of Starlink access
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Oct 16 - US President Donald Trump said on Friday that he did not think either he or Elon Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access in a way that affected its military operations against Russia.

The reduction in services provided by the satellite company interrupted communications with headquarters and caused internet speeds to drop.

Reuters reported on Thursday that the White House approved the reduction in Starshield services.

Trump, speaking to reporters as he left the White House on a trip to Georgia, said neither he nor Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access.

Any limit to Ukraine's access to the Starshield system was not imposed by the United States, Trump added. Starshield was developed by SpaceX specifically for government and national-security customers, particularly the US Department of Defense. Starshield uses the Starlink ​constellation as its backbone.

Trump also he has a good relationship with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.

(Reporting by Trevor Hunnicutt, Steve Holland and Jasper Ward in Washington; Editing by Caitlin Webber)

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq set for steep weekly losses as AI jitters rattle investors
data.description:
By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal

Oct 16 (Reuters) - The benchmark S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end the week in the red, with technology stocks coming under more pressure on Friday over cracks in the AI trade and adding to losses.

The S&P 500 information technology index fell 1.5% and was the biggest drag. Nvidia-backed CoreWeave slid 10.3% on lingering debt concerns. The data centre operator's bonds sold off sharply this week, pushing yields to above 15%.

Semiconductors bore the brunt of the selloff, with the broader chips index dropping 1.8% - set for its steepest eight-session percentage decline since the "Liberation Day" selloff in April 2025.

Most megacap stocks tumbled and brought the Nasdaq close to a one-month low. Meta slipped 2.3% and Microsoft lost 1.8%.

AI stocks have cratered this week over concerns that data centre operators might not turn profitable in time to repay debts, particularly with borrowing costs expected to rise. Worries over rising competition from China also dented sentiment.

"When investors start worrying that AI names are overvalued, they gravitate toward lower-multiple stocks with stable cash flows," said Dennis Dick, founder and market structure analyst at Triple D Trading.

Adding to concerns around AI financing, some current Anthropic investors and prospective investors are weighing a lower valuation for the company in its upcoming IPO, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

At 12:19 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 14.74 points, or 0.03%, to 52,162.95, the S&P 500 lost 43.53 points, or 0.56%, to 7,700.38 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 348.31 points, or 1.30%, to 26,364.72.

Most other S&P 500 sectors rose. The energy index was the biggest percentage gainer, up 1.5%, while the financials index rose 1%. 

Gains in Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase lifted the Dow to its highest level in over a month. The index is set for a weekly advance, with investors rushing to defensive sectors such as healthcare and consumer staples.

"What we're seeing now is money rotating out of a very crowded AI trade and into value names," Dick added.

The S&P 500 was set for its steepest weekly loss since early June, faced with an AI-led rout, mixed bank earnings and inflation data. The Nasdaq eyed its sharpest weekly fall since June 22.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer inflation reports this week have confirmed that price pressures are extending beyond energy products. 

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh also said a spending surge was boosting inflation, but added that the US economy remained resilient and benefited from the AI-driven investment boom.

Markets increasingly expect the Fed to keep interest rates unchanged this month. Barclays now expects 25 basis point hikes each in December and January.

Meanwhile, Tesla failed to hold on to gains from before the bell - as much as 3% - after unveiling a redesigned Roadster, powered by rocket-style thrusters, developed in collaboration with SpaceX. 

Netflix appointed former Disney executive Peter Rice as chief content officer on Thursday. Its shares were down 2.6%.

Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.04-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 1.94-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.

The S&P 500 posted 17 new 52-week highs and no new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 46 new highs and 200 new lows.

(Reporting by Tharuniyaa Lakshmi and Purvi Agarwal in Bengaluru, additional reporting by Vidya Ranganathan; Editing by Joyjeet Das and Shinjini Ganguli)

data.title: ExxonMobil signals $4.5 billion refining earnings boost as margins soar
data.description:
Oct 16 (Reuters) - ExxonMobil ( XOM ) signaled on Friday that higher refining margins during the third quarter could boost its downstream profit by $4.5 billion compared with the previous three months.

Refining margins have soared due to the ongoing Iran war, which has restricted energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The resulting higher fuel prices have created political risks for the administration of US President Donald Trump ahead of the midterm elections in November.

The top US oil producer's expected refining boom could further draw the ire of the president, who complained in August that Exxon and Chevron ( CVX ) were making "too much money".

Exxon's regulatory filing indicates that adjusted net income for the refining business could jump to $8.5 billion, wrote BMO Capital Markets analyst Phillip Jungwirth in a research note. That would be more than double last quarter's profit level.

Here are more details from Exxon's earnings preview:

-- Upstream earnings could take a $1.3 billion hit compared with the second quarter. The average closing Brent benchmark price declined about 5.6% during the third quarter compared with the previous three months, according to LSEG data.

-- Exxon indicated that there were no volume-related disruptions during the quarter stemming from the Iran war.

-- The company's move to divest some upstream assets will boost earnings by $700 million.

-- Exxon will release full third-quarter results on October 30.

-- Exxon shares were up less than 1% in pre-market trading.

(Reporting by Sheila Dang in Houston and Dharna Bafna in Bengaluru; Editing by Anil D'Silva, Joe Bavier and Chizu Nomiyama)
